function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** (in this context) refers to an official authorization or instruction given to someone—typically a financial institution—to act on behalf of another party. In banking and finance, it usually means:

1. **Authorization to Debit/Withdraw Funds:**  
   A customer gives a bank permission to withdraw money from their account automatically—for example, paying recurring bills, payroll deposits, or standing orders.

2. **Standing Order / Direct Debit Mandate:**  
   An agreement where funds are transferred regularly without needing separate instructions each time. It’s common for utilities, subscriptions, mortgages, etc.

3. **Mandated Payment Instructions:**  
   These can include details such as:
   - Account holder’s name & number
   - Bank identifier codes (IBAN/BIC)
   - Frequency (monthly, quarterly, one‑off)
   – Amount limits or specific amounts
   – Effective start/end dates

In short, a mandate tells the bank “you may take/do X amount of Y from Z account at times T.” Once set up, you don’t need to manually authorize each transaction; the mandate automates it under agreed terms.
